subject: Unexpected tail latency and token error surge after model swap
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@cobaltbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: CobaltBridge Ops <ops@cobaltbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 13:10:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden p99 latency + token errors after your upgrade

Marissa —

We rolled the model swap you coordinated (rwin/v4 -> rwin/v4-quant) at 12:45 UTC and immediately saw p99 tail latency jump ~3x and a sharp increase in token-level errors (~0.7% -> 4%). Throughput dropped and our payment pipelines are backing up. Attaching the top-level perf tar.gz and a short sample of failing requests.

Can you confirm whether this rollout changed quantization profiles or runtime kernels? We need an immediate mitigation plan — customers are complaining.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, CobaltBridge

Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency + token errors after your upgrade

Samir — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We’re treating this as an incident.

Immediate steps:
- Triage: engineering to analyze traces and KV cache behavior (Markus + Aditya).
- Mitigation: propose a hot rollback to the previous quant profile or increase replica count to absorb the spike.
- Communications: I’m escalating to execs for credit/comp request handling.

Markus/Aditya — please review the attached perf bundle and flamegraph. Prioritize whether this is a quantization mismatch (precision/regression) or a serving kernel path causing KV thrash. If rollback is safe, indicate command + cluster and I will authorize.

Samir — we’ll update within 30 minutes with proposed action and ETA.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@cobaltbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 14:01:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency + token errors after your upgrade

Quick findings from the initial pass on the perf bundle:
- Several workers hit repeated KV cache evictions when serving batched requests at higher token lengths; eviction storms coincide with p99 spikes.
- A subset of GPU pods reported transient OOMs and restarted; the restart window aligns with the token error surge.
- The quant profile used in the swap differs from the one validated against CobaltBridge long-context workload (we saw different per-layer scales and an aggressive per-tensor clamp).

Attached: flamegraph_worker42.png showing long tails in attention kernel.

Immediate recommendation: rollback to the previous quant profile for the primary region and temporarily force the older kernel path for attention on the affected fleet; this should restore latency and reduce token errors. If rollback isn’t acceptable, increase replica count + temporary request throttling to avoid eviction storms.

I can prepare the rollback playbook; need authorization to run it.

– Markus (serving runtime)

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@cobaltbridge.com>

Confirming the business impact: we’ve seen a 22% drop in processed payments in the past 20 minutes and downstream queues are growing. We need a fix now; rollback is preferred if it can be done with low risk. We are also formally requesting temporary account credits for remediation window — CC’ing finance/ops.

I’ve uploaded a second log bundle (sample_requests.json) with the failing request ids. If you need anything else from our side, call me: +1-415-555-0123.

Samir

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency + token errors after your upgrade

Action plan I can execute within the hour:
1) Safe rollback path: pin model -> old quant profile v2.3 -> step traffic via canary (5% -> 50% -> 100%) over 20 minutes. This uses existing config and is reversible.
2) Fast mitigation if rollback blocked: increase replicas by 40% for affected autoscaling group and enable the attention kernel fallback to reduce KV pressure.
3) Throttle non-critical inference routes and enable circuit breaker for long requests (>2k tokens) until stable.

I’m prepared to execute the rollback now upon Marissa’s authorization. I’ll run the notebooked rollback playbook (incident_playbook_v3.md) and post progress to PD-INC-9953.

Aditya
